entries.message: threw, so the navigation was canceled — a throwing guard fails closed.

entries.message: <a route href="{href}"> points outside the app's base ("{base}"). Clicking it works, because the router re-bases the URL it writes — but the href itself is wrong anywhere the router is not involved: a new tab, a copied link, a crawler.
entries.fix: Write it as "{base}{pathname}" or relative to the <base>. `resolve()` already returns the mounted path.

entries.message: `{option}` is not an initRouter option, so it was ignored.

entries.message: expected a path or a { name, params } object and received {received}.
navigating to {path} threw, so the view was left as it was.
entries.fix: A link click has nobody to reject to: listen for `vera:route-error` (it bubbles, composed) to handle it; the error is printed beside this line.

entries.message: nothing matched "{path}", so the navigation did nothing. A link with `route` has already had its click canceled by then.
entries.fix: Add the route, or a catch-all `/*rest`, which sorts last however it is declared.

entries.message: the route "{path}" is nested, so its view is looked for inside the one its parent rendered into — and no [view="{variant}"] was found there.
entries.fix: A parent's template has to render the outlet its children route into.

entries.message: nothing is wired to render a route, so navigation changes the URL and paints nothing.
entries.fix: Wire the router itself alongside the renderer — `wire([renderer, router])` — or hand it one directly with `setRouterRenderer(render)`.

entries.message: needs an element and a view — without a view there is no outlet, so every navigation would do nothing.
entries.fix: initRouter(element, { view }) — the view is an element or the name of a [view] outlet.

entries.message: a redirect loop at {path} — ten redirects in one navigation, so it was stopped.
entries.fix: Check the routes whose `redirect` lead back to each other.

entries.message: navigate("{target}") from "{prior}" resolved to "{bare}" — a relative path replaces the last segment, like a relative href, and here that segment was a route param ("{last}").
entries.fix: For the SIBLING "{bare}" this is right. For the child "{prior}/{target}", use a named route — `navigate({ name })` fills params from the current route — or the absolute path.
`@verajs/renderer` exports it as `renderInto` — or pass the module to `wire` instead, which is what `wire([renderer, router])` does.

entries.message: `{key}` is not a route option, so it was ignored on "{path}".
entries.fix: The options are {known} — anything else belongs in `meta`, which every guard and action reads off the snapshot.
